newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr eases vs yen on Summers remarks, finds support.
newsitem.headline: Dlr eases vs yen on Summers remarks, finds support.

text.p: *Dollar dipped against yen in mid-morning Tokyo on comments by Deputy U.S. Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers, but was well-supported at 125.50 yen by buying interest from Japanese investors and securities houses, dealers said.

*Summers said domestic-led growth in Japan crucial to avoid trade friction and U.S. would react strongly if trade pacts violated. He told Economic Strategy Institute that Japan faces profound challenges such as serious financial strains, ageing population and economy overburdened by regulation.
*Dollar later fell below 125.50 yen, mainly due to active sales from U.S. fund operators, said a European bank dealer.
*Stop-loss dollar sales triggered around 125.50 yen, with buying by Japanese investors insufficient to halt slide.
*Dealers said Summers' remarks weighed on dollar.
*Currency manager at Japanese bank said news that Japan's surplus with United States rose also weighed on dollar.
*Trade surplus with United States, often source of trade friction, rose 11.2 percent in March from year earlier to 379.83 billion yen, Japan finance ministry said.
*Dollar briefly inched up following smaller-than-expected overall Japanese customs-cleared trade surplus, but failed to move above 126 yen with offers lined up around that level.
*Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus slid 26.8 percent in March from a year earlier to 818.34 billion yen.
*Japanese interbank dealers and speculators, joined by U.S. operators, were behind dollar sales later.
*Comments from Japanese and U.S. authorities on Wednesday still having impact and fuelling intervention fears in Asia, weighing on dollar, dealers said.
